security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, multilingual text, benign URLs, or routine shell output capture. Confirmed risks include local moves and symlinks, broad persistent Bash authorization, unvalidated path placeholders, and third-party CDN resources without integrity checks. No prompt injection or credential-exfiltration intent was found. Static review was capped at 400/859 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 459 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The allow command grants broad persistent Bash permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove wildcard Git and ~/.claude permissions. Request confirmation for each move, symlink, settings edit, commit, and push operation.

remediation.issue: Skill names and configured paths are inserted into shell commands without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only a strict skill-name pattern, quote every path, resolve canonical paths, and verify source and destination containment before changes.

remediation.issue: Migration moves the source before proving the complete workflow succeeds.
remediation.suggestion: Copy to a temporary destination, verify content, create the link atomically, and keep a documented rollback path until the user confirms success.

remediation.issue: Generated pages load executable JavaScript from a third-party CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor dependencies or add exact versions, Subresource Integrity hashes, crossorigin attributes, and a restrictive Content Security Policy.

remediation.issue: Git pushes can publish local skill content to a remote repository.
remediation.suggestion: Show the remote, branch, and staged files, scan for secrets, and require explicit confirmation immediately before every push.

content.user_title: Share Local Skills Through Git Repositories
content.value_statement: Local skills are difficult to version and publish. This skill migrates them into Git repositories and generates documentation and marketplace metadata.
actual_capabilities: Finds local skills under standard Claude configuration directories.
Moves a selected skill into a configured code repository.
Creates a symlink so Claude Code can continue discovering the migrated skill.
Initializes Git, configures a remote, commits changes, and optionally pushes.
Generates multilingual README files and a GitHub Pages documentation site.
Creates Claude Code plugin manifests and updates marketplace metadata.
limitations: It modifies local files, symlinks, Git repositories, and Claude Code configuration.
Remote repository creation and authentication must already be available.
Generated documentation depends on repository conventions described by the skill.
The bundled verification script checks structure, not content accuracy or secret exposure.

use_cases.title: Publish a Personal Skill
use_cases.description: Move one local skill into a Git repository while preserving Claude Code discovery.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Team Skill Collection
use_cases.description: Add skills to a shared repository with manifests, README tables, and consistent documentation.

use_cases.title: Build a Public Skill Catalog
use_cases.description: Generate multilingual GitHub Pages documentation and marketplace metadata for an open source collection.

prompt_templates.title: List Local Skills
prompt_templates.prompt: List local skills available for migration. Show each source path and identify existing symlinks. Do not modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Without Publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate [skill-name] into my configured skills repository. Create the compatibility symlink, but do not add a remote or push.

prompt_templates.title: Publish to a Specific Remote
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate [skill-name] to [remote-url]. Show the destination, staged files, and remote before requesting confirmation to push.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Multilingual Catalog
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate documentation for [repository] in English, Chinese, and Japanese. Preserve existing package scripts and use [domain] only after confirmation.

output_examples.output: Found three local skills. Two are available for migration, and one already links to the configured repository.
Moved release-notes into the skills repository, created its compatibility symlink, initialized version tracking, and skipped remote publication.
Generated both language variants, updated the skill catalog, created the documentation site, and reported the files awaiting review.

best_practices: Review the resolved source, destination, remote, branch, and staged files before approving changes.
Back up local skills and keep Git recovery information until the migrated skill works through its symlink.
Scan skill content for credentials and private data before any commit or push.
anti_patterns: Do not grant wildcard Bash permissions for convenience.
Do not accept unvalidated skill names, paths, domains, or remote URLs.
Do not push automatically after migration or documentation generation.

faq.question: Does this skill create a remote repository?
faq.answer: No. The remote must exist, and local authentication must permit access before a push can succeed.

faq.question: Will Claude Code still find a migrated skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow creates a symlink from the original skills directory to the repository location.

faq.question: Can I migrate without publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. Skip remote configuration and review the local repository before any later push.

faq.question: Which documentation languages are supported?
faq.answer: The documented workflow supports English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and user-specified language codes.

faq.question: Does it overwrite an existing destination?
faq.answer: The instructions require an error when the target exists, but users should still keep a backup.

faq.question: What permissions does it need?
faq.answer: It needs scoped access to selected skill files, destination paths, Git commands, and configuration fields used by the requested operation.
